title: Marcos joins AFP boodle fight

blocks.text: President Marcos joins members of the AFP Council of Sergeants Major yesterday in a boodle fight, a traditional military communal meal that highlights equality, camaraderie and unity among senior enlisted leaders, officers and troops.

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos capped his loaded schedule yesterday by joining a boodle fight with the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Council of Sergeants Major, providing him an opportunity to listen to and speak directly with the soldiers.
The President arrived at Camp Aguinaldo at around 6 p.m. for the boodle fight, a communal way of eating and sharing food piled onto banana leaves, using one’s hands.
Palace press officer Claire Castro said the meal symbolized unity, equality, respect and good relations between the civilian government and the military.
“The President wants to connect, listen, recognize and care for the defenders of the nation,” Castro said in a media briefing.
The event also sought to emphasize the importance of soldiers’ welfare and morale and to acknowledge their efforts to secure Filipinos and the country.
